summary: Gumboot Mountain lookout, Gifford Pinchot NF, Skamania County WA: 1920 cupola cabin, L-4 cab 1931 per sources; 1927 fire threat; now gone, removal year not given.

facts.design: Cupola cabin (1920); L-4 cab (1931), per WillhiteWeb and the Forest Fire Lookout Association
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Former Fire Lookout Sites register and the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no removal year given

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb's 2017 visit: final road overgrown and rough, hike up to one mile or so; a forest road dead-ended in washouts at the bottom of the mountain

events.note: About 7,000 pounds of lookout-house parts carried by horse toward Gum Boot on the Yacolt burn, per the Oregonian
Cabin completed by October 1920 by John Huffman and John Meyers of the Forest Service; 3.5-mile trail made to the summit; cupola cabin per the Forest Fire Lookout Association
Siouxon fire district: crews pulled out; Gumboot station believed likely to burn; instruments removed and houses abandoned (Statesman Journal, as quoted on the Washington Lookouts page)
L-4 cab built, per WillhiteWeb and the Forest Fire Lookout Association; the register gives 1931 as the build year and does not mention 1920
Panorama photos taken at 15 feet above the ground
Registered June 24, 2012 as FFLOS US 1322, WA 222; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the build to 1931 with an L-4 cab and omits the 1920 cabin. WillhiteWeb and the Forest Fire Lookout Association describe a cupola cabin finished in 1920, then an L-4 cab in 1931. The story reports both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Story sources: the story says 'About 7,000 pounds' from the Oregonian via Washington Lookouts; the 7,000 figure is also on WillhiteWeb as '7000 pounds'. The Washington Lookouts page has an 1927 Statesman Journal item, which the story treats as a report of belief, not confirmation that the cabin burned. No source gives a removal year. WillhiteWeb gives elevation as '3,8564 feet' (typo) and the register says 3,910 ft; the register figure is used. The brief's kind 'ground' is not checked by any source: sources describe a cabin and a garage at the summit but never say whether it stood on a tower, so the story says 'cabin' and avoids 'tower'. No staffing found. Access level omitted: no source states one. The 2017 photo captions are quoted but not interpreted. Brief record is consistent with sources except the build date (no build event was in the brief's record). Lat/lon in brief matches the register.
